title: Derived germs commute with semilinear transport on a proper geometric fibre
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum $p,a,q,k_0,k$ of [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ in the chosen algebraic closure $\Qlb$, and $\Lambda\in\{E,\Qlb\}$. Use the rationalized and common-stage categories of [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi, def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients]. Let $Y_0$ be proper of finite type over $k_0$ [def-weil-proper-morphism], put $Y=Y_0\times_{k_0}k$, $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$, and write $a_Y:Y\to s$. Put $h=\operatorname{Spec}(\gamma)$ and $g=\operatorname{id}_{Y_0}\times h$, where $\gamma=(c\mapsto c^q)^{-1}$ [def-weil-frobenius-detailed]. Write $P_r=L(g^r)^*$ and $Q_r=L(h^r)^*$ for derived pullback [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. All pullback-composition comparisons are the scalar localizations of [lem-pod-integral-pullback-composition], and at $\Qlb$ are represented at a common finite field stage.

For $M\in D^b_c(Y,\Lambda)$ put $C(M)=R\Gamma_c(Y,M)$ [def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology]. Use the identity compactification of $a_Y$ to identify this with $R\Gamma(Y,M)$ and to form $\tau_{c,M}:C(M)\to C(P_1M)$ [lem-pod-proper-coincidence-frobenius, def-weil-frobenius-cohomology-transport]. For a $k$-point $z:s\to Y$ (a geometric point of [def-weil-geometric-point]), put $C_z(M)=\operatorname{Fib}_s(Lz^*M)$ [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point]. Let $e_z^M:C(M)\to C_z(M)$ be the derived germ: through $R\Gamma_c\cong R\Gamma$, it is obtained by applying $\operatorname{Fib}_sLz^*$ to the counit $La_Y^*Ra_{Y*}M\to M$ [fix-prop-adjunctions], using $a_Yz=\operatorname{id}_s$ and the canonical composition comparisons.

For $r\geq1$ let $T(z)=gz h^{-1}$ and $z_r=T^r(z)=g^rz h^{-r}$, which are $k$-points. The equality $g^rz=z_rh^r$ and the specified pullback-composition comparisons give
$$b_{r,z,M}:Q_rLz_r^*M\xrightarrow{\sim}Lz^*P_rM.$$
Let $d_r:P_r\xrightarrow{\sim}P_1^{\,r}$ be the iterated composition comparison. Define
$$\tau^{[r]}_{c,M}=C(d_{r,M}^{-1})\circ\tau_{c,P_1^{r-1}M}\circ\cdots\circ\tau_{c,M}:C(M)\longrightarrow C(P_rM).$$
For $N\in D^b_c(s,\Lambda)$ let $I_N^{[r]}:\operatorname{Fib}_s(N)\to\operatorname{Fib}_s(Q_rN)$ be the composite of the $r$ point transports $\iota_N,\iota_{Q_1N},\ldots,\iota_{Q_1^{r-1}N}$ [def-weil-frobenius-point-transport], followed by the specified composition comparison.

Then the following identity holds in $D^b_{\mathrm{fd}}(\Lambda)$, naturally in $M$, for every $r\geq1$ and every $k$-point $z$:
$$e_z^{P_rM}\circ\tau^{[r]}_{c,M}=\operatorname{Fib}_s(b_{r,z,M})\circ I_{Lz_r^*M}^{[r]}\circ e_{z_r}^M.$$
No Weil structure on $M$ is assumed. In particular the formula concerns the specified exchange-mate/point-transport composite, not an unspecified identification of coefficient spaces.

proof.text: Use the identity compactification. Write $R=Ra_{Y*}$, $V=\operatorname{Fib}_s$, $\iota$ for the point transport of the statement, $\mathcal E_M=\operatorname{FrEx}_{Y,*}(M):Q_1RM\to RP_1M$ for the direct-image exchange, so that $\tau_M=V(\mathcal E_M)\iota_{RM}$ is the ordinary transport of [def-weil-frobenius-cohomology-transport]. By [lem-pod-proper-coincidence-frobenius](2), $\kappa_M$ identifies $C(M)$ with $VRM$ and $\tau_{c,M}$ with $\tau_M$. Naturality of $\kappa$ also identifies $C(d_{r,M}^{-1})$ with $VR(d_{r,M}^{-1})$. Put $Z_z=Lz^*$, let $\varepsilon:La_Y^*R\to\mathrm{id}$ be the counit of the statement and $u_z:Z_zLa_Y^*\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathrm{id}$ the specified comparison for $a_Yz=\mathrm{id}_s$. The germ in the statement becomes $V(v_z^M)$, where $v_z^M=Z_z(\varepsilon_M)u_z(RM)^{-1}:RM\to Z_zM$. Thus it suffices to prove the ordinary-cohomology identity with these factors. Properness is used here; $g,h$ remain the given semilinear scheme automorphisms.

source.place: (1.1.7), (1.1.10)--(1.1.14), pp. 150--153; agent assembly using the completed germ square and conditional iteration/coefficient-descent lemmas.

proof.text: For every finite coefficient field $E$, [lem-a1-integral-semilinear-germ-square] gives naturality of $v_z$ and the identity $v_z^{PM}\mathcal E_M=b_{1,z,M}Q(v_{z_1}^M)$ for all integral objects and all $k$-points. Its comparisons, counit and exchange are exactly those fixed in the statement, formed on strict coefficient systems before taking derived inverse limit. Its moving-point assertion gives $z_j=g^jzh^{-j}$ as $k$-points with $gz_j=z_{j+1}h$.

source.place: (1.1.7), (1.1.10)--(1.1.14), pp. 150--153; agent assembly using the completed germ square and conditional iteration/coefficient-descent lemmas.

proof.text: Apply [lem-a1-semilinear-germ-iteration-descent] to this family of one-step integral identities. Its definitions give the same $d_r$, $b_{r,z,M}$, $\tau_M^{[r]}$ and $I_N^{[r]}$ as in the question. Its contracted equality, including rational and common-stage coefficients, is $e_z^{P_rM}\tau_M^{[r]}=V(b_{r,z,M})I_{Z_{z_r}M}^{[r]}e_{z_r}^M$, naturally in $M$. Under step 1 every factor is the required compact-support factor; this proves the stated formula for every $r\ge1$. Both cited results allow arbitrary constructible $M$ without a Weil structure.
